description: A stream read by DML INSIDE a stored procedure must advance its offset when the transaction commits, exactly as the same DML would at top level. The consuming-DML window used to be opened only by the string entry point, but a BEGIN...END body dispatches its statements through the visitor directly, so a procedure's INSERT ... SELECT FROM stream read the stream WITHOUT registering it: the offset never advanced and each re-CALL of a loader procedure re-processed everything it had already loaded. The window now opens at the dispatch point every path shares. Pinned with an explicit COMMIT in the body, with the CALL's own autocommit, with a NESTED call where a second pass must load only its delta, with a SIBLING stream that keeps its own offset, and with the mid-procedure FLUSH idiom, which needs both halves of the fix - DDL inside the body implicitly commits the open transaction so the flush consumes at its own point, and commit-time consumption is SCOPED to what each read saw so the flush cannot swallow rows inserted after it. The same scoping is pinned at top level in an explicit transaction. And a plain SELECT inside a procedure does NOT consume. Converted 1:1 from stream/StreamConsumptionInProcedureTest (now retired).
